PASCAL, EVOQUE and SAPIEN M3 differentiated body of clinical evidence continues to expand</font></div><div style="text-indent:4.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:174%;text-decoration:underline">2026 Outlook</font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:9.65pt">Increasing total company constant currency</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">2</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%"> sales growth guidance&#58; 10% to 11% from 9% to 11%</font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:9.65pt">Increasing TAVR constant currency</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">2</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%"> sales growth guidance&#58; 8% to 9% from 7% to 9%</font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:9.65pt">Increasing TMTT sales guidance&#58; $760 to $780 million from $740 to $780 million</font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:9.65pt">Reaffirming adjusted EPS guidance of $2.95 to $3.05, growing 17% at midpoint</font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:9.65pt">Expected clinical presentations at TCT&#58; PROGRESS and CLASP IITR </font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:9.65pt">Expected Q4 approvals of PASCAL tricuspid indication in U.S. and next-generation PASCAL with Capture Clarity in U.S. and Europe</font></div><div style="text-indent:4.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8220;We delivered stronger-than-expected second quarter sales growth of 12.5%. As Edwards continues to invest in new structural heart therapies and expand adoption globally, our results increasingly reflect the strength of our comprehensive portfolio and agile execution, with growth supported by therapies across TAVR, mitral, tricuspid and surgical, as well as meaningful contributions from each of the regions,&#8221; said Bernard Zovighian, Edwards&#8217; CEO. &#8220;Today, our company profile has evolved to include multiple strategic platforms across multiple regions that will support durable growth, which gives us confidence in our target of approximately 10% total company sales growth, on average, over the longer term. Our strategic focus coupled with our commitment to early innovation enables us to deliver meaningful impact for patients worldwide.&#8221;</font></div><div style="height:27pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:right"><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:174%;text-decoration:underline">Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR)</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">In the second quarter, the company reported TAVR sales of $1.3 billion, which grew 11.3% compared to the prior year, or 10.5% on a constant currency basis. Globally, procedural growth benefited from sustained clinical momentum and the evidence supporting proactive disease management of severe aortic stenosis (AS). At the same time, treatment decisions continued to be shaped by the long-term differentiation of our SAPIEN platform. Edwards&#8217; growth rates were similar in the U.S. and outside of the U.S. Growth benefitted from the exit of a competitor in Q2 2025 and compelling long-term SAPIEN durability data. Average selling prices were stable globally. </font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">At the recent New York Valves conference, a new PARTNER 3 trial sub-analysis of the SAPIEN platform at 7 years reinforced the best-in-class valve performance and long-term durability of Edwards TAVR. Further, a 5-year analysis presented from the EARLY TAVR trial adds to the growing evidence supporting a shift toward treating AS earlier in the disease pathway. Also at New York Valves, the PROGRESS trial baseline characteristics presentation provided new insights into the heterogeneous nature of moderate aortic stenosis patients. The clinical community will learn more about the clinical relevance of treating these patients with TAVR when the PROGRESS trial results are presented at TCT later this year. </font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">In the U.S., procedure growth continued to benefit from a heightened focus on TAVR therapy as the clinical community continues to incorporate recent evidence supporting proactive disease management. Edwards&#8217; competitive position in the U.S. increased modestly year-over-year, enabled by continued adoption of its SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA platform. The Centers for Medicare &#38; Medicaid Services (CMS) continues to advance the reconsideration of the National Coverage Determination (NCD) for TAVR, with a final decision memo expected in September. This update has the potential to advance TAVR therapy for Medicare beneficiaries with aortic stenosis.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Outside of the U.S., the company continues to see strong adoption of the SAPIEN platform. In Europe, updated ESC and EACTS guidelines are helping shape clinical discussions around earlier intervention and proactive disease management, further reinforcing the role of TAVR across a broader patient population. Edwards&#8217; competitive position also increased modestly year-over-year in Europe. In Japan, Edwards was encouraged by the growth and continued adoption of its SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA platform.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:174%;text-decoration:underline">Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Therapies (TMTT)</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Second quarter TMTT sales of $195.9 million increased 47.3% compared to the prior year, or 44.8% on a constant currency basis. Results were driven by the company&#8217;s differentiated portfolio of repair and replacement therapies to treat mitral and tricuspid diseases. Globally, mitral and tricuspid procedure growth remained in the double digits.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Adoption of Edwards&#8217; PASCAL system continues to increase, reflecting strong physician enthusiasm for its differentiated design and clinical outcomes, as well as the significant unmet needs of patients with mitral and tricuspid valve diseases. The company continues to expect that its next-</font></div><div style="height:27pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">2</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:right"><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">generation PASCAL with Capture Clarity technology for both mitral and tricuspid patients in the U.S. and Europe will be approved in the fourth quarter. Also in the fourth quarter, Edwards continues to expect CLASP IITR trial results to be presented at TCT, and the launch of the PASCAL system in the U.S. for tricuspid patients.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">The EVOQUE system is a significant growth platform for TMTT and continues to scale in the U.S. and Europe. Edwards is increasing patient access to and driving further adoption of the EVOQUE system by expanding into new centers, deepening utilization in existing centers and streamlining patient screening processes. The company expects the value of its growing body of clinical evidence will further increase with time, as demonstrated by recent reductions in all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalizations, and will support continued physician adoption and expansion of access for patients with tricuspid regurgitation.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">The company&#8217;s early experience with the SAPIEN M3 system validates the significant need for mitral replacement solutions for patients who are not well-suited for mitral TEER and demonstrates excellent clinical outcomes for patients. Edwards is continuing with a measured launch of the SAPIEN M3 system in the U.S. and Europe, steadily opening new centers and supporting sites as they build procedural experience.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:174%;text-decoration:underline">Surgical</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">In Surgical, second quarter global sales of $284 million increased 6.5% compared to the prior year, or 5.0% on a constant currency basis, driven by continued adoption of the company&#8217;s RESILIA tissue therapies including the INSPIRIS, MITRIS and KONECT devices, which provide extended durability for patients. </font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">At the recent AATS conference, 10-year data from the COMMENCE trial, studying the long-term durability of Edwards&#8217; best-in-class RESILIA tissue, were presented. The results showed favorable 10-year freedom from structural valve deterioration, or SVD, and a very low rate of SVD-related reoperation regardless of age, even in a relatively young cohort.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">The company also received U.S. approval for ECLIPTIS, its surgical left atrial appendage system, and is planning for a measured rollout later this year, supported by a continued focus on procedural excellence and patient outcomes.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:174%;text-decoration:underline">Additional Financial Results</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">For the quarter, gross profit margin was 77.5%, or 77.6% adjusted, consistent with the same period last year and driven by foreign exchange headwinds offset by lower manufacturing expenses. The company now expects gross profit margin to be at the lower end of its full-year 78% to 79% gross margin guidance, driven by the impacts of foreign exchange through its hedging program.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Selling, general and administrative expenses in the second quarter were $561 million, or 32.2% of sales, compared to 32.8% of sales in the prior year. This was in line with the company&#8217;s expectations and reflects continued investment in resources to support patient care as well as a higher translation of the company&#8217;s OUS expense base from the weakening dollar.  Research and Development (R&#38;D) expenses </font></div><div style="height:27pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">3</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:right"><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">in the second quarter were $279 million, or 16.0% of sales, compared to 18.0% in the prior year. This decrease in R&#38;D as a percentage of sales and increase in total expense reflects Edwards&#8217; growing revenue and strategic prioritization of investments in its expanding structural heart portfolio. The company continues to expect R&#38;D expense as a percentage of sales to be approximately 17% in 2026.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Operating profit margin in the second quarter was 29.5%, or 30.0% adjusted. Adjusted EPS was $0.78 and benefited from better-than-expected topline performance and planned phasing of strategic investments in R&#38;D and SG&#38;A throughout the year. In 2026, Edwards continues to expect full-year operating profit margin to be at the high end of the company&#8217;s original 28% to 29% guidance range, resulting in approximately 150 basis points of constant currency operating margin expansion for the full year.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Edwards now expects its 2026 effective tax rate, excluding special items, to be at the high end of its previous range of 16% to 19%. This reflects an expectation that side-by-side safe-harbor taxation legislation related to Pillar Two does not come into effect before the end of the year. The company&#8217;s tax rate is also impacted by changes to California law restricting the usage of R&#38;D credits.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Cash and cash equivalents were approximately </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">$2.9 billion</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%"> </font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">as of June&#160;30, 2026. Total debt was approximately $600 million.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Edwards has approximately $1.5 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:174%;text-decoration:underline">Outlook</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Based on the company&#8217;s second quarter performance, Edwards is increasing its full-year 2026 sales growth rate guidance to 10% to 11% from 9% to 11%, TAVR product group sales growth guidance to 8% to 9% from 7% to 9%, and TMTT product group sales guidance to $760 to $780 million from $740 to $780 million. Edwards now expects full-year total company sales of $6.6 billion to $6.9 billion and TAVR sales of $4.75 billion to $5.0 billion at current exchange rates. Edwards is also reaffirming adjusted EPS guidance of $2.95 to $3.05, despite now assuming the company&#8217;s effective tax rate will be at the high end of the original 16% to 19% range. For the third quarter of 2026, the company projects total sales to be between $1.63 and $1.71 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.71 to $0.77.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="height:27pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">4</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:right"><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:232%;text-decoration:underline">About Edwards Lifesciences</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:232%">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Edwards Lifesciences is the leading global structural heart innovation company, driven by a passion to improve patient lives. Through breakthrough technologies, world-class evidence and partnerships with clinicians and healthcare stakeholders, our employees are inspired by our patient-focused culture to deliver life-changing innovations to those who need them most. Discover more at www.edwards.com and follow us on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram and YouTube.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:232%;text-decoration:underline">Conference Call and Webcast Information</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:232%">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">The company will be hosting a conference call today at 2&#58;00&#160;p.m. PT to discuss its second quarter results.&#160;To participate in the conference call, dial (877) 704-2848 or (201) 389-0893. style="text-align:right"><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">EDWARDS LIFESCIENCES CORPORATION</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Non-GAAP Financial Information</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">To supplement the consolidated financial results prepared in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;), the Company uses non-GAAP historical financial measures. Management makes adjustments to the GAAP measures for items (both charges and gains) that (a) do not reflect the core operational activities of the Company, (b) are commonly adjusted within the Company&#8217;s industry to enhance comparability of the Company&#8217;s financial results with those of its peer group, or (c) are inconsistent in amount or frequency between periods (albeit such items are monitored and controlled with equal diligence relative to core operations). The Company uses the terms &#8220;adjusted&#8221; and &#8220;constant currency&#8221; when referring to non-GAAP sales from continuing operations and sales growth information, respectively, which excludes currency exchange rate fluctuations and newly acquired products. The Company uses the term &#8220;adjusted&#8221; to also exclude certain litigation expenses, amortization of intangible assets, a gain on remeasurement of previously held interest upon business combinations, loss on impairment, impact of tax law change on R&#38;D credit, and separation costs.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Management uses non-GAAP financial measures internally for strategic decision making, forecasting future results, and evaluating current performance. These non-GAAP financial measures are used in addition to, and in conjunction with, results presented in accordance with GAAP and reflect an additional way of viewing aspects of the Company's operations by investors that, when viewed with its GAAP results, provide a more complete understanding of factors and trends affecting the Company's business and facilitate comparability to historical periods.  </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Non-GAAP financial measures are not prepared in accordance with GAAP&#59; therefore, the information is not necessarily comparable to other companies and should be considered as a supplement to, and not as a substitute for, or superior to, the corresponding measures calculated in accordance with GAAP. A reconciliation of non-GAAP historical financial measures to the most comparable GAAP measure is provided in the tables below.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Fluctuations in currency exchange rates impact the comparative results and sales growth rates of the Company's underlying business. Management believes that excluding the impact of currency exchange rate fluctuations from its sales growth provides investors a more useful comparison to historical financial results. The impact of the fluctuations has been detailed in the &#8220;Reconciliation of Sales by Product Group and Region.&#8221;  </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Guidance for sales and sales growth rates is provided on a &#8220;constant currency basis,&#8221; and projections for diluted earnings per share, net income and growth, gross profit margin, and taxes are also provided on a non-GAAP basis, as adjusted, for the items identified above due to the inherent difficulty in forecasting such items without unreasonable efforts. The Company is not able to provide a reconciliation of the non-GAAP guidance to comparable GAAP measures due to the unknown effect, timing, and potential significance of special charges or gains, and management's inability to forecast charges associated with future transactions and initiatives. </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">The items described below are adjustments to the GAAP financial results in the reconciliations that follow&#58;</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Certain Litigation Expenses</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> - The Company incurred certain litigation expenses of $37.1&#160;million and $10.9&#160;million in the first quarter of 2026 and 2025, respectively, and $6.3&#160;million and $15.5&#160;million for the second quarter of 2026 and 2025, respectively. Such expenses relate to intellectual property litigation, settlements, contingencies, and external legal costs.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Amortization of Intangible Assets</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> - The Company recorded amortization expense related to developed technology and patents in the amount of $3.3 million and $1.4&#160;million in the first quarter of 2026 and 2025, respectively, and $3.2&#160;million and $1.8&#160;million in the second quarter of 2026 and 2025, respectively,</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Separation Costs</font><font other professional advisory services related to the sale of Critical Care.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New of an investee and a $19.9&#160;million</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">gain in the second quarter of 2026 to remeasure its previously held interest upon consolidation of one of its variable interest entities (&#8220;VIE&#8221;).</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New investments not being recoverable and $40.0&#160;million in the second quarter of 2026 due to the Company's determination to not exercise an option to acquire one of its VIE.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="height:40.5pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div periods.</font></div><div style="height:40.5pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font
